findings.issue: Card sprite derivation is implemented twice (also app/src/lib/data.ts:290); a sprite bug fix in speciesCardsFromRefs covers moves/types/abilities lists but silently leaves the home list wrong.
findings.suggestion: Have getHomeCatalog build its entries through speciesCardsFromRefs, or extract a single spriteForPokemon(record) helper used by both.

findings.issue: Three filter handlers each duplicate 'set signal, reset page, window.history.replaceState(homeUrl(...))' and sync the URL by hand, bypassing the Qwik City router (back/forward won't re-sync the signals).
findings.suggestion: One applyFilter(patch) helper in the route; consider useNavigate()/useLocation() so the router stays the single owner of URL state.

findings.issue: The '<count> Pokémon' + <ul class=card-grid> + PokemonCard list block is copy-pasted across the moves, abilities and types detail routes (app/src/routes/abilities/[name]/index.tsx:53, app/src/routes/types/[name]/index.tsx:85).
findings.suggestion: Extract a PokemonCardList (or CardListSection) component that takes the cards array and heading, so list behaviour/presentation changes land once.

findings.issue: TypeBadgeLink exists (app/src/components/ui.tsx:41) but the identical badge-link markup is inlined here, at app/src/routes/moves/[name]/index.tsx:57 and app/src/routes/types/[name]/index.tsx:73.
findings.suggestion: Use TypeBadgeLink everywhere; a badge change (markup, href scheme, CSS class) then lands in one file.

findings.issue: The not-found flow ({notFound:true} flags plus matching head branches) is re-implemented in four routes and serves HTTP 200 for missing resources; Qwik City's documented approach is throwing ev.error(404, ...) from the loader with a shared 404.tsx.
findings.suggestion: Wrap resource loading in one helper (or use ServerError/ev.error) and a single custom 404 route, collapsing four copies of the pattern and producing a real 404 status.

findings.issue: data.ts mixes server-only data access with presentation helpers (humanize :97, displayDex :129, formatValue :133 — imported by client components at app/src/components/ui.tsx:3) and route-level query parsing (parseHomeQuery :330), making the module a grab-bag and blurring where an edit belongs.
findings.suggestion: Split into lib/api.ts (fetch + cache), lib/format.ts (pure helpers) and keep query parsing in the route that owns it.

findings.issue: The data seam is untyped (record: any, Promise<any> returns at :297/:306) despite strict tsconfig, so API shape changes surface as runtime breakage rather than compile errors.
findings.suggestion: Declare minimal interfaces for the API records actually consumed (name/names, sprites, types, moves) instead of any.

findings.issue: The SpeciesCard shape is redeclared inline here instead of importing the exported type from lib/data.ts.
findings.suggestion: Import SpeciesCard so shape changes are caught by the compiler in all consumers.

findings.issue: All styling for five pages lives in one 700-line global stylesheet with feature-specific selectors (.hidden-ability :278, .move-links, .relations), so feature removal or class renames leave dead CSS and risk global name collisions; Qwik's idiomatic option is scoped styles in components.
findings.suggestion: Move per-page/per-component styles into the owning components with Qwik's scoped <style> blocks, keeping only tokens and layout globals in global.css.

findings.issue: The Game select navigates with window.location.assign, forcing a full page reload instead of a SPA navigation.
findings.suggestion: Use Qwik City's useNavigate() to update the ?game param so navigation stays router-managed.

summary: The app is layered unusually well for its size: routes → one server-side data module → API, with components that only know prop objects, so data-source and cross-resource changes land in a single file. The cost shows up in repeated small boilerplate at the route layer — duplicated sprite derivation, copy-pasted card-list and not-found blocks, and inline type-badge markup — meaning the classic bug fix or feature extension touches several near-identical files. Net: pleasant to extend along existing seams, mediocre when a change must sweep every instance of a repeated pattern.
